# FirecREST Agentic Workbench — self-installation guide for AI agents

> Machine-oriented, self-contained instructions that let a coding agent (Claude Code,
> Codex, Hermes, …) install the FirecREST v2 demo stack and the FirecREST MCP server of
> this repository on a Linux host, optionally publish the MCP endpoint behind Cloudflare
> Access, and verify every step. Human-oriented reference: docs/DEPLOYMENT-VPS.md.
> Workstation variant (full workbench with MetaMCP, DocMind, Multica): docs/local-env.md,
> docs/ENVIRONMENT.md.

Repository: https://github.com/VadaLinux/firecrest-agentic-workbench
Upstream FirecREST v2: https://github.com/eth-cscs/firecrest-v2 (pinned tag 2.6.1)
Python client: pyfirecrest 3.10.0. MCP SDK: mcp >=2,<3.

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## 0. Rules for the agent (read first, follow throughout)

1. Execute the phases in order. Every phase ends with a VERIFY block. If a verification
   fails, STOP, report the exact output, and do not continue.
2. HUMAN GATES. Before any command marked [SUDO] or [PUBLIC], show the human exactly what
   will run and wait for explicit approval. Approval of one gate does not cover the next.
3. Never print, log or commit secrets (client secrets, tokens, .env contents). When a secret
   must be written to a file, write it without echoing it, and report only "written".
4. Never bind the MCP server to 0.0.0.0. It has no authentication of its own.
5. Never publish the MCP endpoint without Cloudflare Access in front of it (phase 7 order:
   Access application first, tunnel route second, external check third).
6. Be idempotent: before creating anything, check whether it already exists and report it.
7. Do not modify the upstream firecrest-v2 clone. Deviations live in this repo's
   docs/patches/ and are applied by scripts/workbench-up.sh.
8. Report, at the end, the commit deployed, the state of each unit, and the result of every
   VERIFY block.

## 1. Inputs to collect from the human before starting

| Variable | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `OP_USER` | Linux user that owns and runs everything | current user |
| `REPO` | path of this repository | `$HOME/Sviluppo/firecrest-agentic-workbench` |
| `V2` | path of the upstream firecrest-v2 clone | `$HOME/Sviluppo/firecrest-demo/firecrest-v2` |
| `PUBLISH` | publish the MCP endpoint on the internet? `yes`/`no` | `no` |
| `PUBLIC_HOST` | public hostname, only if `PUBLISH=yes` | none; must be a bare DNS name, letters/digits/hyphens, NO underscore |
| `ALLOWED_EMAILS` | e-mail addresses allowed by Cloudflare Access | none |
| `CF_MODE` | who configures Cloudflare: `human` (dashboard) or `api` (scoped token) | `human` |

Validate `PUBLIC_HOST` with: `^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?(\.[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]*[a-z0-9])?)+$`.
A hostname containing `_` is invalid for DNS and public TLS certificates: ask for another.

## 2. Phase 1 — Preflight (read-only)

```bash
uname -a; cat /etc/os-release | head -3
command -v git docker gh curl python3 || true
docker compose version
id -nG "$USER" | tr ' ' '\n' | grep -x docker || echo "NOT IN docker GROUP"
command -v uv || ls ~/.local/bin/uv
systemctl --version | head -1
df -h "$HOME" | tail -1; free -g | sed -n 2p
for p in 8000 5678 8765 18080 9090 6820 2222 5665 5666; do ss -Htln "sport = :$p" | grep -q . && echo "PORT $p BUSY"; done
sudo -n true 2>/dev/null && echo "sudo: non-interactive OK" || echo "sudo: needs password/approval"
command -v ufw && sudo -n ufw status 2>/dev/null | head -5
```

VERIFY: Docker and Compose present; user in `docker` group; `uv` present (if not, install
with `curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh` after human approval); at least
10 GB free disk and 4 GB RAM; none of the ports busy. If a port is busy, STOP and report
which process owns it (`sudo ss -Htlnp "sport = :<port>"`).

## 3. Phase 2 — Clone

```bash
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$REPO")" "$(dirname "$V2")"
[ -d "$REPO/.git" ] || git clone https://github.com/VadaLinux/firecrest-agentic-workbench.git "$REPO"
git -C "$REPO" pull --ff-only
[ -d "$V2/.git" ] || git clone https://github.com/eth-cscs/firecrest-v2.git "$V2"
git -C "$V2" fetch --tags -q && git -C "$V2" checkout -q 2.6.1
```

VERIFY:
```bash
git -C "$REPO" rev-parse --short HEAD        # record it
git -C "$V2" describe --tags                 # 2.6.1
git -C "$REPO" status --porcelain | wc -l    # 0
```

## 4. Phase 3 — Configure the MCP server

The demo uses the public test client of the upstream compose stack. Its secret is published
in the upstream user guide; read it from there without printing it.

```bash
cd "$REPO/firecrest-mcp"
if [ -e .env ]; then echo ".env exists: not overwritten"; else
  SEC=$(grep -o 'client_secret=[A-Za-z0-9_-]*' "$V2/docs/user_guide/README.md" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)
  [ -n "$SEC" ] || { echo "demo secret not found in upstream guide: ask the human"; exit 1; }
  umask 077
  cat > .env <<EOF
FIRECREST_API_VERSION=v2
FIRECREST_V2_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8000
FIRECREST_V2_TOKEN_URL=http://localhost:18080/auth/realms/kcrealm/protocol/openid-connect/token
FIRECREST_V2_CLIENT_ID=firecrest-test-client
FIRECREST_V2_CLIENT_SECRET=$SEC
FIRECREST_V2_SYSTEM=cluster-slurm-api
FIRECREST_V2_VERIFY_SSL=true
EOF
  unset SEC
fi
if [ "$PUBLISH" = yes ]; then
  grep -q '^FIRECREST_MCP_PUBLIC_HOST=' .env || echo "FIRECREST_MCP_PUBLIC_HOST=$PUBLIC_HOST" >> .env
fi
chmod 600 .env
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
[ -x .venv/bin/python ] || uv venv -q .venv
uv pip install -q --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt
mkdir -p logs downloads
```

VERIFY:
```bash
stat -c '%a' .env                                          # 600
git -C "$REPO" check-ignore -q firecrest-mcp/.env && echo ignored
grep -c '=.' .env                                          # count only, never cat .env
.venv/bin/python -c 'import mcp, firecrest, httpx; print("deps ok")'
.venv/bin/python server.py --help | head -1                # usage: server.py ...
```

## 5. Phase 4 — Install the systemd units [SUDO]

The unit files in `systemd/` are written for user `master` and paths under
`/home/master/Sviluppo`. If `OP_USER`, `REPO` or `V2` differ, render adapted copies first:

```bash
R=$(mktemp -d)
for u in firecrest-demo-v2 firecrest-mcp-v2; do
  sed -e "s#/home/master/Sviluppo/firecrest-agentic-workbench#$REPO#g" \
      -e "s#/home/master/Sviluppo/firecrest-demo/firecrest-v2#$V2#g" \
      -e "s#/home/master#$HOME#g" \
      -e "s#^User=master#User=$OP_USER#" -e "s#^Group=master#Group=$(id -gn "$OP_USER")#" \
      "$REPO/systemd/$u.service" > "$R/$u.service"
done
grep -nE '^(User|Group|WorkingDirectory|ExecStart|ReadWritePaths|Environment)=' "$R"/*.service
```

Show the rendered lines to the human, then, after approval:

```bash
for u in firecrest-demo-v2 firecrest-mcp-v2; do
  [ -e /etc/systemd/system/$u.service ] && echo "$u already installed: compare before replacing"
  sudo install -o root -g root -m 644 "$R/$u.service" /etc/systemd/system/$u.service
done
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemd-analyze verify /etc/systemd/system/firecrest-demo-v2.service /etc/systemd/system/firecrest-mcp-v2.service
sudo systemctl enable firecrest-demo-v2.service firecrest-mcp-v2.service
```

VERIFY: `systemd-analyze verify` prints no error for these two units;
`systemctl is-enabled firecrest-demo-v2 firecrest-mcp-v2` prints `enabled` twice.
Note: enabled units start automatically at the next boot.

## 6. Phase 5 — Start and smoke-test FirecREST v2 [SUDO]

```bash
sudo systemctl start --no-block firecrest-demo-v2
until s=$(systemctl is-active firecrest-demo-v2); [ "$s" != activating ]; do sleep 10; done; echo "$s"
```

The first start pulls and builds images and can take 5–15 minutes.

VERIFY:
```bash
systemctl is-active firecrest-demo-v2                                     # active
docker ps --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}\t{{.Ports}}'                   # firecrest, slurm (healthy), keycloak (healthy); ALL ports start with 127.0.0.1: (incl. 5678 = debugpy, must never be public)
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:8000/status/systems        # 401
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:18080/auth/realms/kcrealm  # 200
cd "$REPO" && uv run --quiet --with pyfirecrest==3.10.0 python scripts/smoke_local.py
# last line: OK — token, systems, submit, poll, output all verified.
```

The warning "firecrest-mcp is NOT listening on :8765" in the unit log is expected until
phase 6.

## 7. Phase 6 — Start and test the MCP server [SUDO]

```bash
sudo systemctl start firecrest-mcp-v2
sleep 5; systemctl is-active firecrest-mcp-v2                # active
ss -Htln 'sport = :8765'                                     # 127.0.0.1:8765 ONLY
```

If `ss` shows `0.0.0.0` or `*`, STOP immediately and run `sudo systemctl stop firecrest-mcp-v2`.

Host allowlist check:
```bash
INIT='{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"initialize","params":{"protocolVersion":"2025-06-18","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"probe","version":"0"}}}'
for h in 127.0.0.1:8765 "$PUBLIC_HOST" evil.example.com; do
  [ -z "$h" ] && continue
  o=; [ "$h" = "$PUBLIC_HOST" ] && o="-H Origin:https://$h"
  printf '%s -> ' "$h"; curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp \
    -H "Host: $h" $o -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H 'Accept: application/json, text/event-stream' -d "$INIT"
done
# expected: 127.0.0.1 -> 200, PUBLIC_HOST -> 200, evil.example.com -> 421
```

End-to-end MCP test. Save as a script OUTSIDE the repository and run it with the server's
venv (mcp SDK 2.x API: `streamable_http_client` yields two streams; tools expose `input_schema`):

```python
import asyncio
from mcp import ClientSession
from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamable_http_client

def text(r):
    return " ".join(getattr(c, "text", str(c)) for c in r.content)

async def main():
    async with streamable_http_client("http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp") as (read, write):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as s:
            await s.initialize()
            print([t.name for t in (await s.list_tools()).tools])
            r = await s.call_tool("submit_job", {
                "system": "cluster-slurm-api", "template": "hello",
                "parameters": {"nodes": 1, "time_minutes": 5, "partition": "part01",
                               "job_name": "install-check", "message": "install-ok"},
                "approved_by": "installer-check", "actor": "installer-agent",
                "working_directory": "/home/fireuser"})
            print(text(r))

asyncio.run(main())
```

VERIFY: six tools are listed (`submit_job`, `cancel_job`, `get_job_status`, `list_files`,
`download_file`, `get_job_log`); `submit_job` returns `"ok": true` with a `jobid`;
`get_job_status` on that id reaches `COMPLETED`; `get_job_log` shows
`hello-from-fcagent install-ok`; `download_file` of `/home/fireuser/slurm-<jobid>.out` saves
into `firecrest-mcp/downloads/`; `firecrest-mcp/logs/audit.jsonl` has an `"outcome": "submitted"` line.

Guardrails, expected behaviour (do not "fix" them):
- a free-form `script` without `template` is refused (`FirecRESTError`);
- `approved_by` must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$`, otherwise `GuardrailDenied` / `approved_by_required`;
- v2 needs an absolute `working_directory`;
- limits come from `config/limits.yaml` (max 2 nodes, 30 minutes, partitions part01/part02).

If `PUBLISH=no`, the installation is complete here. Agents on the same host use
`http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp`.

## 8. Phase 7 — Publish behind Cloudflare Access [PUBLIC] (only if PUBLISH=yes)

Strict order: 7.1 → 7.2 → 7.3 → 7.4. Never create the tunnel route before the Access
application exists: in that window the MCP server is open to the internet.

### 7.1 Login method
Zero Trust → Settings → Authentication → Login methods: One-time PIN enabled.
(API: `GET /accounts/{account}/access/identity_providers` must list type `onetimepin`.)

### 7.2 Access application (Self-hosted)
- name `FirecREST MCP`; session 24h; domain `PUBLIC_HOST`, path empty;
- one policy: decision `allow`, include = one `email` rule per address in `ALLOWED_EMAILS`;
- never `bypass`, never `everyone`, never IP-based rules.

API variant (`CF_MODE=api`, token with Access: Apps and Policies Edit, Cloudflare Tunnel Edit,
DNS Edit on the zone; token stored in a 0600 file and never printed):
```
POST /client/v4/accounts/{account}/access/apps
{"name":"FirecREST MCP","type":"self_hosted","domain":"<PUBLIC_HOST>","session_duration":"24h",
 "app_launcher_visible":false,
 "policies":[{"name":"Operators","decision":"allow","precedence":1,
              "include":[{"email":{"email":"<addr1>"}},{"email":{"email":"<addr2>"}}]}]}
```
Record the returned `aud`. The account id is in `GET /zones?name=<zone>` → `result[0].account.id`.

### 7.3 Tunnel
The human installs `cloudflared` as a system service with a token-based tunnel (dashboard:
Networks → Tunnels → Create → Cloudflared → run the shown `cloudflared service install <token>`).
Then one public hostname route:
- hostname `PUBLIC_HOST`, path empty, service `http://127.0.0.1:8765`;
- HTTP Host header: empty;
- Access → enforce JWT validation: on, application `FirecREST MCP`.

Resulting remotely-managed config (API: `PUT /accounts/{account}/cfd_tunnel/{tunnel}/configurations`;
back up the current config with GET first):
```json
{"config":{"ingress":[
  {"hostname":"<PUBLIC_HOST>","service":"http://127.0.0.1:8765",
   "originRequest":{"access":{"required":true,"teamName":"<team>","audTag":["<aud>"]}}},
  {"service":"http_status:404"}]}}
```
`<team>` is the subdomain of `<team>.cloudflareaccess.com`, visible in the `Location` header of
any redirect produced by step 7.4. A proxied DNS CNAME `PUBLIC_HOST → <tunnel-id>.cfargotunnel.com`
is created by the dashboard route.

### 7.4 External verification (from a machine that is NOT the host)
```bash
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code} %{redirect_url}\n' "https://$PUBLIC_HOST/mcp"
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST "https://$PUBLIC_HOST/mcp" -d '{}'
```
VERIFY: both return `302` to `https://<team>.cloudflareaccess.com/cdn-cgi/access/login/...`.
Then on the host:
```bash
journalctl -u firecrest-mcp-v2 --since '-5 min' -o cat | grep 'HTTP/1.1' | grep -v '127.0.0.1:'
```
must print NOTHING. If any line appears, anonymous traffic reaches the server: treat it as an
incident, run `sudo systemctl stop cloudflared`, and fix the Access application before retrying.
Note: right after creating the Access application, allow up to a minute for propagation and repeat.

Human check: open `https://PUBLIC_HOST/mcp` in a browser, log in with an allowed e-mail and the
PIN. Expected body: `{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":null,"error":{"code":-32600,"message":"Bad Request: Missing session ID"}}`.

## 9. Phase 8 — Connect an MCP client

Claude Code (on the human's machine):
```bash
claude mcp add --transport http --scope user firecrest-v2 "https://$PUBLIC_HOST/mcp"
# in Claude Code: /mcp → firecrest-v2 → Authenticate → Access login in the browser
```
Headless clients cannot do the PIN login: create an Access service token and a second policy with
decision `non_identity` (Service Auth) on the same application; the client sends
`CF-Access-Client-Id` and `CF-Access-Client-Secret`.

## 10. Final report template

```
Deployed commit: <sha>   Upstream firecrest-v2: 2.6.1
Units: firecrest-demo-v2=<state> firecrest-mcp-v2=<state> cloudflared=<state|n/a>
Ports: all loopback = <yes/no>
Smoke test: <OK/FAIL>   MCP e2e: jobid=<id> state=<state>
Allowlist: 127.0.0.1=<code> public=<code> foreign=<code>
Access (external): GET=<code> POST=<code> anonymous-at-origin=<0/n>
Human gates approved: <list>
```

## 11. Operations and removal (short)

- Status: `systemctl is-active firecrest-demo-v2 firecrest-mcp-v2 cloudflared`
- Logs: `journalctl -u firecrest-mcp-v2 -f`; audit: `firecrest-mcp/logs/audit.jsonl`
- After code or .env changes: `git pull --ff-only`, reinstall requirements, `sudo systemctl restart firecrest-mcp-v2`
- Stop the stack: `sudo systemctl stop firecrest-mcp-v2; (cd "$V2" && docker compose down)` — never `-v`
- Remove: `sudo systemctl disable --now firecrest-mcp-v2 firecrest-demo-v2`, `docker compose down` in `$V2`,
  delete both files from `/etc/systemd/system/`, `sudo systemctl daemon-reload`; in Cloudflare delete the
  tunnel route first, then the Access application.

Full details, troubleshooting table and change history: docs/DEPLOYMENT-VPS.md.
